target.name: runtime-installed IWRAM interrupt dispatcher
target.role: the machine's interrupt entry: an IE/IF priority scan, a pre-handler acknowledge, a 14-entry vector call in Thumb state and a full restore, installed into the BIOS IRQ vector pointer at 0x03007FFC
target.notes: THE SECOND RUNTIME-INSTALLED TARGET, AND THE FIRST WHOSE ENTRY IS A HARDWARE VECTOR RATHER THAN A CALL SITE. The block the boot DMA3 copy installs is entered by sixteen routes, not thirteen: the thirteen Thumb-to-ARM veneers carry the two block-memory entries and the eleven other library routines, and three further IWRAM addresses are stored as ROM literal-pool words - 0x0803E36C = 0x03000868, 0x0803F3BC = 0x03000AE0, 0x0803F434 = 0x03000B6C - each read by exactly one Thumb instruction. This unit is the third of those. THE ENTRY IS THE BIOS IRQ VECTOR POINTER 0x03007FFC, and it is never stored as a literal anywhere in the image: the 26-byte Thumb routine at 0x0803F3DA computes it as 0x03007FC0 + 0x3C, then sets REG_IE = 0x2000, REG_IME = 1 and REG_DISPSTAT = 0x18. THE DISPATCHER ITSELF runs ARM from 0x087B8510 to the `bx lr` at 0x087B8638: it saves spsr/IME/IE, re-enables IME, computes IE & IF, scans the interrupt bits in a FIXED PRIORITY ORDER - bit 10 first, then 7, 6, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, which is all fourteen GBA IRQ bits - acknowledges the served source with ONE 32-bit store that clears the bit in IE's half and sets it in IF's half BEFORE the handler runs, ORs the served mask into a 16-bit software word at the table's own end (0x03000FE8), switches to system mode, and calls vector_table[offset/4] through `bx r0` with r4 = the ARM resume address 0x03000C7C and lr = the ODD address 0x03000C99. The handler returns in Thumb state into the halfword 0x4720 at 0x03000C98 (`bx r4`), which is why the ARM walk cannot see the return path and why the unit's own boundary derivation has to follow `add r4, pc, #0`. THE VECTOR TABLE is 14 words at IWRAM 0x03000FB0 and its extent is proved from what follows it, not from its shape: the dispatcher reads the pending halfword at base + 0x38, so the table ends exactly there. In the ROM every entry is 0x0803F3D9, i.e. the one-instruction Thumb stub 0x0803F3D8 whose whole body is `bx lr`, and the table IS populated at run time - ROM 0x0803F21A's function dereferences the data word 0x087B6EDC, which holds 0x03000FB0, and stores 0x03000AE0 into slot 10 while enabling REG_IE bit 10, which is the same bit the priority chain reads at byte offset 0x28. THIRTEEN of the fourteen tests can reach a slot; the last one settles on a SELF-BRANCH instead, so a pending bit 13 spins forever and the final slot is never selected - reproduced, not repaired. The first test settles on the ORR and so SKIPS the IE clear, which no other test does. The `ip` register is 0x9F for that first test and 0x1F for every later one, which is the only difference in the CPSR write. NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN C, and modelled as environment calls rather than omitted: the SPSR read and write, the CPSR mode switch, and the ARM-to-Thumb-to-ARM return. Everything memory-visible - which bit is acknowledged, in what order, which slot is called, what is pushed and restored, and the spin - is reconstructed exactly. See docs/LIFT_IWRAM_DISPATCH.md.

boundary_evidence.method: aligned chain-walk from each entry, following local branches

functions.role: IRQ dispatch: IE/IF priority scan, acknowledge, vector call, restore

iwram_dispatch.method: the stored-pointer census reads every 2-byte-aligned window of the image; a stored word counts as an entry only when some instruction's pc-relative read lands on it; the dispatcher, its priority chain and its vector table are decoded from its own instruction words

stored_pointer_route.method: every 4-byte window at every 2-byte-aligned offset of the image, kept when its value lies in [0x03000000, 0x03001004); a value counts as referenced when an instruction's pc-relative read lands on its slot and that instruction lies below the structural map's code end (0x08060000)

irq.reachability_note: the fourteen tests select byte offsets 0x00..0x30, so thirteen of the table's slots are reachable. The last test's taken branch is a self-branch instead of the handler path, so bit 13 spins and the slot at the final offset is never entered.

acknowledgement.operation: one 32-bit store acknowledges IF and unmasks IE

vector_table.slot_count_derived_from: the dispatcher reads a halfword at the table base + 0x38, so the table ends where that word begins: (0x03000FE8 - 0x03000FB0) / 4

software_pending_word.role: the dispatcher ORs the served bit into this halfword before it calls the handler; nothing else in the block reads it and its consumer was not found, so its purpose is UNKNOWN

default_handler.note: the install routine is the NEXT function, at ROM 0x0803F3DA; it is not a vector slot

install_path.installer_is_named_by_a_stored_word_note: the 4-byte value 0x0803F3DA does not occur anywhere in the image, so the only way to reach the routine is a branch - which is why a search for the address as a pointer reports, wrongly, that the BIOS IRQ vector is never installed
install_path.bios_irq_vector_pointer_method: for every instruction that pc-relatively reads the dispatcher's own address literal, the enclosing Thumb function is walked with registers tracked through literal loads, and each store of that value through a literal base is reported with its computed destination - the BIOS IRQ vector pointer is never stored as a literal, it is computed as 0x03007FC0 + 0x3C
install_path.vector_table_write_method: the table base 0x03000FB0 is stored in a DATA word, not in code; the derivation finds every instruction that loads the address of such a word, follows the register through one dereference, and reports each store through it

callgraph.method: aligned recursive descent from the veneer destinations and from every stored pointer an instruction actually loads; an address is a function leader when it is a call or branch target that is not also reached by fallthrough

ads_match.detail: an ARM Developer Suite 1.2 installation is present on this machine but the licence file it ships licenses a different product, so the ARM compilers cannot be run. No compile has been attempted and no configuration has been tested. The installation is located through ADS12_ROOT.
required_to_unblock: a licensed ADS 1.2 installation, with ADS12_ROOT pointing at it

verdicts_are_independent: SEMANTIC, MODERN_BUILD and ADS_MATCH answer different questions and none is evidence for another. A passing modern build says nothing about the original compiler; a passing semantic run only removes one class of error.

identity.why_not: the original translation unit was built by ARM Developer Suite 1.2 (the surviving command line names tcpp). GCC is a different compiler with a different code generator, so its output cannot establish anything about ADS 1.2.

target_support.detail: compiled and disassembled a probe function for ARM7TDMI Thumb: 2 instruction(s), r0 written and a return present

literal_pools.interpretation: the original's literals are accounted for by the words the unit declares; the modern build pools differently, which is a structural consequence of the compiler rather than a defect in the reconstruction. It is also why a function with a literal load cannot be compared standalone.

comparison.match_claim_note: MEASUREMENT ONLY. This compares a modern GCC build against the cartridge. A modern compiler is not the original compiler, so a difference here is expected and proves nothing; an identity here would also prove nothing about ADS 1.2. ADS_MATCH stays BLOCKED.
